review_scope: P4 Switch first-release BMv2/P4Runtime 1.4.1 implementation, public-boundary startup, fault, performance, soak, supply-chain, findings, and operational-completion evidence

findings.title: P4 qualification aggregation did not machine-prove the append-only findings registry or operational completion
findings.resolution: Added the Switch module to the shared append-only findings contract, bound the registry digest and open counts into qualification evidence, derived operational completion from exact mandatory gates, real runtime startup, the formal 3,600-second soak and open-P0=0, and added negative tests that prevent a missing gate or open P0 from producing Module Complete.

findings.title: Formal supply-chain inputs in the system temporary directory could expire during the one-hour soak
findings.resolution: The formal runner now validates both source archives against their locked filename, size and SHA-256 and atomically snapshots them into the run-specific durable output directory before any long-running test. Supply-chain verification consumes only those immutable snapshots, so temporary-file cleanup cannot invalidate a run after the soak.

findings.title: The formal source snapshot included generated C++ and Rust build trees
findings.resolution: The canonical supply source-tree archive now excludes generated build, target, dist, cache, egg-info and coverage outputs while retaining repository source, contracts, deployment assets and tests. This removes tens of gigabytes of non-source content without weakening source or secret scanning.

findings.title: Formal supply could start without enough free disk for offline bundles and rebuilds
findings.resolution: The qualification profile now freezes a 32 GiB minimum free-space budget. The runner checks it before long-running tests and again before supply; an insufficient environment fails closed with a typed supply reason instead of exhausting the filesystem during bundle creation.
